node.title: Re: To count number of files created yesterday in a directory
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [ajy],

Please use tags around your code so that it gets displayed properly. See also [id://174051].

Note that the core module [doc://File::stat] makes [doc://stat] (which [beech] already recommended) a bit easier to use. At the top of your program, use File::stat;, then to get a file's creation time as a UNIX timestamp, you simply need to call stat($filename)->ctime. The Perl function [doc://time] will give you the current time as a UNIX timestamp, so you just need to compare them.

Since you're using [doc://readdir], note that it's necessary to prepend the directory name to the filenames that [doc://readdir] returns. In your example, at the top of the program say use File::Spec::Functions qw/catfile/;, then in the loop you just need to say my $filename = catfile($dir, $FILE);. Also, it's possible to use [doc://File::Spec]'s no_upwards function to skip the directories . and .. instead of the regex /^\.\.?/ (Update: Although, note that this regex also causes filenames beginning with a dot to be skipped, not sure if that's what you want?).

There are other ways to list files in a directory, for example, there's [doc://glob] (note that by default, that skips files whose name begin with a dot), or maybe [mod://Path::Class::Dir]'s children function.

One more note: you should use warnings; at the top of your script, and check the return value of [doc://opendir] for errors, and I'd recommend lexical file/directory handles, as in opendir(my $dirhandle, $dir) or die "opendir $dir: $!"; - then use $dirhandle instead of DIR.

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
